name: Zostel Srinagar
summary: A backpacker hostel in the Nishat area, a short walk from the eastern shore of Dal Lake, with dorm beds, private rooms and a rooftop looking over the lake. It is the easiest social base in Srinagar for students and solo travellers.
body: Zostel Srinagar sits in Nishat, near the Mughal garden of the same name and about a five-minute walk from Dal Lake. It offers dorms and simple private rooms, a common area and a rooftop terrace with views across the water to the Hari Parbat side of the city. The location is quieter than Dal Gate and close to the Mughal gardens, though you will need autos or cabs to reach the old city and Lal Chowk.

It suits solo travellers, students and young couples who want company and local tips without paying hotel rates. Expect hostel standards: shared bathrooms in dorms, limited food, and a relaxed crowd. Book ahead in April to June, when beds fill quickly, and confirm heating if you visit between November and March.
why: One of the cheapest reliable beds in Srinagar
Walking distance to Dal Lake and Nishat Bagh
Easy place to meet other travellers and share cabs
price_band: ₹600–1,200 for a dorm bed; ₹2,000–4,000 for a private double (indicative)

faqs.q: Is Zostel Srinagar close to Dal Lake?
faqs.a: Yes, it is in the Nishat area, about a five-minute walk from the eastern shore of Dal Lake and close to Nishat Bagh. The main ghats at Dal Gate are a short auto or cab ride away along the Boulevard.

faqs.q: Is Zostel Srinagar safe for solo women?
faqs.a: Zostel properties are popular with solo women travellers and usually offer female dorms. As anywhere in Srinagar, avoid isolated walks after dark and use registered cabs. Check current room types when booking.

faqs.q: Does Zostel Srinagar have heating in winter?
faqs.a: Heating varies by room and season. If you plan to visit between November and March, confirm heaters or extra blankets with the property before booking, as nights fall below freezing.

name: JKTDC Huts and Cottages, Pahalgam
summary: The Jammu and Kashmir Tourism Development Corporation runs cottages and huts in Pahalgam, set among pines near the Lidder. They are the most reliable government stay in town, good value for families sharing a multi-room cottage.
body: JKTDC's Pahalgam property offers cottages from one bedroom upwards, with kitchenettes or sitting rooms in some units, spread over wooded grounds near the river. Rooms are plain and functional, and standards vary between units, but the setting is calm and central. Families and groups get the best value by booking a multi-bedroom cottage and sharing.

Book directly on the official JKTDC website, where rates and availability are listed, and confirm what is included: heating, hot water and meals are not always standard. In peak months from April to June and during the Amarnath Yatra, book well ahead. Off-season, JKTDC sometimes offers discounts.
why: Government-run, transparent pricing booked online
Pine and river setting close to the bazaar
Multi-room cottages good for families and groups
price_band: ₹2,800–10,000 a night for a cottage unit (indicative)

faqs.q: How do I book JKTDC huts in Pahalgam?
faqs.a: Book on the official JKTDC website, which lists units, rates and availability, or contact JKTDC offices in Srinagar. Avoid third-party sellers asking for advance payments in cash. Carry the confirmation and your ID.

faqs.q: Are meals included at JKTDC Pahalgam?
faqs.a: Usually not by default. Some units have kitchenettes, and JKTDC or nearby restaurants provide meals. Confirm meal options when booking, especially off-season when services are limited.

faqs.q: Are JKTDC huts heated in winter?
faqs.a: Heating depends on the unit and season. Ask before booking for December to March, and expect to pay extra for heaters. Bring warm sleepwear regardless.

name: JKTDC Tourist Bungalow and Huts, Dawar
summary: JKTDC's accommodation at Dawar, the main township of Gurez, includes a tourist bungalow with rooms and log huts near the Kishanganga. It is basic but one of the few organised stays in the valley, with views towards Habba Khatoon peak.
body: In a valley with very few hotels, the JKTDC property at Dawar offers simple rooms and log huts run by the government tourism corporation. Facilities are modest: beds with warm blankets, attached or shared bathrooms depending on the unit, and limited food service. The location is central for walks around Dawar and trips to Tulail.

Book through the official JKTDC website or offices, and confirm before travelling, because the valley is open only from about late May to November and services start and stop with the season. Carry cash, a torch and warm layers. If it is full, family homestays in Dawar make a good alternative.
why: Government stay in a valley with few organised options
Central location in Dawar near the river
Views towards Habba Khatoon peak
price_band: ₹1,500–4,000 a night for a room or hut (indicative)

faqs.q: Is the JKTDC stay in Gurez open all year?
faqs.a: No. Gurez is cut off by snow on the Razdan Pass for about six months, so the property operates in season, roughly late May to November. Confirm dates and availability before you travel.

faqs.q: What facilities does JKTDC Dawar have?
faqs.a: Expect simple rooms and huts with warm bedding, and basic food service. Hot water and power can be intermittent. Treat it as a clean, safe base rather than a hotel.

faqs.q: Are there alternatives to JKTDC in Gurez?
faqs.a: Yes, several family homestays and guesthouses in Dawar and nearby villages, and seasonal riverside camps. Homestays include home-cooked meals and are a good way to meet local families.

name: Ahdoos Hotel
summary: A long-established city hotel on Residency Road in central Srinagar, best known for its restaurant, one of the valley's oldest and a reference for Kashmiri wazwan. Rooms are comfortable and practical, close to Lal Chowk and a few minutes from Dal Lake.
body: Ahdoos stands on Residency Road in the commercial heart of Srinagar, within walking distance of Lal Chowk and the Jhelum bridges, and a short drive from Dal Gate. The hotel has around two dozen air-conditioned rooms, and its restaurant, dating back about a century, is where many Srinagar families go for wazwan dishes such as rista, rogan josh and gushtaba served à la carte.

It suits travellers who want a central hotel with good Kashmiri food and easy access to shops, banks and the old city, rather than a lakeside view. Street noise is part of the package, so ask for a room away from the road. It is a good base for day trips by shared Sumo, which leave from nearby stands.
why: Central location near Lal Chowk and the Jhelum
In-house restaurant famous for Kashmiri wazwan
Practical base for day trips and the old city

faqs.q: Is Ahdoos Hotel close to Dal Lake?
faqs.a: It is in central Srinagar on Residency Road, about five to ten minutes by car from Dal Gate and the Boulevard. It does not have lake views, but it is close to Lal Chowk, the Jhelum and the old city.

faqs.q: Can non-guests eat at Ahdoos restaurant?
faqs.a: Yes, the restaurant is open to the public and popular with locals for wazwan dishes. Lunch and dinner get busy on weekends and holidays, so go early or book ahead.

faqs.q: Is Ahdoos suitable for families?
faqs.a: Yes, families use it as a central, comfortable base. Ask for quieter rooms away from the main road, and confirm room sizes and extra bed options when booking.

name: Hotel Highlands Park
summary: A heritage hotel from the early 1960s on a rise above the Gulmarg meadow, with a main lodge and separate cottage-style buildings, Kashmiri decor and a lounge bar long popular with skiers. It has character the newer hotels lack.
body: Highlands Park sits on a hill facing Apharwat, a short ride or about ten minutes' walk from the gondola base. Guest rooms are in a central building and several cottage-style blocks, with Kashmiri woodwork, sitting areas and refurbished bathrooms. The restaurant serves Kashmiri dishes including wazwan alongside international food, and the lounge bar is a social hub in the ski season.

It suits travellers who want an old-school mountain lodge with atmosphere rather than a modern resort. Skiers like the easy access to beginner slopes in winter; summer visitors enjoy the gardens and views. Book early for the ski season and Christmas, and confirm heating details for winter stays.
why: Heritage atmosphere dating from the early 1960s
Close to the gondola and beginner ski slopes
Kashmiri woodwork, gardens and a lively lounge in winter

faqs.q: How far is Highlands Park from the Gulmarg Gondola?
faqs.a: About 2 km by road, roughly ten minutes on foot or a short drive. In winter some guests ski down to the gondola area. Confirm current transfers with the hotel.

faqs.q: Is Highlands Park good for skiers?
faqs.a: Yes, it has long been popular with skiers for its location near beginner slopes, social bar and warm rooms. Book well ahead for January to March and the Christmas period.

faqs.q: Is Highlands Park open in summer?
faqs.a: It operates in summer as well as winter, with meadow and mountain views. Check current availability and any seasonal closures when booking.

name: The Pahalgam Hotel
summary: One of Pahalgam's oldest hotels, established in the early 1930s, set in gardens above the Lidder with rooms and suites looking towards the river and snow peaks. A comfortable, central choice with old-hill-station character.
body: The Pahalgam Hotel stands on about two acres close to the main bazaar, with lawns and views over the Lidder river to the forested slopes and snow peaks beyond. It has a mix of rooms and suites, many with river views, and a restaurant serving Kashmiri and Indian food. Its long history makes it a familiar name for Indian families who have visited Pahalgam over generations.

It suits families and couples who want comfort, a central location and gardens rather than a modern resort. Union taxis for Aru, Betaab Valley and Chandanwari leave from the nearby stand. Confirm current room categories, heating for cold months and meal plans when booking, and book early for April to June.
why: Long-established hotel close to the bazaar
Gardens and river views over the Lidder
Comfortable for families and seniors

faqs.q: Is The Pahalgam Hotel close to the market?
faqs.a: Yes, it is close to the main bazaar and taxi stand, so you can walk to shops and restaurants and pick up union taxis for sightseeing. Ask for a river-facing room for the best views.

faqs.q: Is The Pahalgam Hotel suitable for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes, its central location, gardens and level access to many rooms suit seniors. Confirm room location and stairs when booking, and ask about heating in spring and autumn.

faqs.q: Does The Pahalgam Hotel stay open in winter?
faqs.a: Many Pahalgam hotels reduce operations in deep winter. Check current status and heating arrangements before booking a stay between December and February.

name: The LaLiT Grand Palace Srinagar
summary: The former Gulab Bhavan, a summer palace completed in 1910 for Maharaja Pratap Singh, set in large lawns with chinar trees above Dal Lake. Restored and run by The LaLiT group, it is Srinagar's grandest place to stay.
body: Gulab Bhavan was completed in 1910 as a summer residence for the Dogra Maharaja Pratap Singh, overlooking Dal Lake from the slopes of the Zabarwan in eastern Srinagar. Its stone facade with a colonnaded verandah mixes European palace details with Indian planning. The palace became a hotel in the 1950s and was restored and extended later, taking its present name in 2008.

Stay in the palace wing for heritage rooms or the newer wing for modern comforts. The lawns, among the largest in the city, are shaded by old chinar trees, which turn red in October. It suits signature travellers, honeymooners and families who want space and calm, close to the Boulevard and the Mughal gardens.
why: A real Maharaja's palace from 1910
Large lawns and chinar trees above Dal Lake
Close to the Boulevard and Mughal gardens

faqs.q: Is The LaLiT Srinagar a real palace?
faqs.a: Yes. It is the former Gulab Bhavan, completed in 1910 as a summer residence of Maharaja Pratap Singh, later converted into a hotel and restored. The original palace building is part of the hotel today.

faqs.q: Does The LaLiT Srinagar have lake views?
faqs.a: The palace stands on high ground above Dal Lake, and many rooms and the lawns look towards the lake. Request a lake-facing room in the palace wing when booking and confirm the view category.

faqs.q: When is the best time to stay at The LaLiT Srinagar?
faqs.a: April and May for spring gardens and tulips, and October for chinar colours on the lawns. Winter is quiet and cold but beautiful with snow on the Zabarwan. Book early for the tulip season.

name: The Khyber Himalayan Resort & Spa
summary: Gulmarg's top resort, opened in December 2012, with rooms and private cottages looking over the meadow and pine forest to the Apharwat ridge, and a large spa. In winter it is the most sought-after base for skiers.
body: The Khyber sits among pines above the Gulmarg meadow, near the gondola, with interiors that draw on Kashmiri woodwork, carpets and textiles. It has around 80 rooms plus a few private cottages, a spa, and restaurants serving Kashmiri and international food. Views from many rooms take in the meadow, forest and the Apharwat ridge.

It is the obvious choice for signature trips to Gulmarg, especially in the ski season, when it fills early for late December to February. In summer it makes a quiet, luxurious base for the gondola and meadow walks. Book well ahead for winter and confirm transfers from Srinagar and ski storage.
why: Gulmarg's most complete luxury resort
Close to the gondola, with meadow and mountain views
Spa and warm, well-run rooms in deep winter

faqs.q: How far is The Khyber from the Gulmarg Gondola?
faqs.a: It is close to the gondola base, a short walk or shuttle ride depending on snow. Confirm current transfer arrangements with the resort, especially in deep winter.

faqs.q: When should I book The Khyber Gulmarg?
faqs.a: Book months ahead for late December to February, when skiers and New Year visitors fill it. Summer from May to June is also busy. Shoulder months like September and October are easier.

faqs.q: Is The Khyber good for families?
faqs.a: Yes, larger rooms and cottages suit families, and the resort has restaurants and a spa on site. Ask about connecting rooms and child policies when booking.

name: Welcomhotel by ITC Hotels, Pine N Peak, Pahalgam
summary: A five-star hotel in Pahalgam on the Aru road side of town, run under ITC's Welcomhotel brand, with around 68 rooms, suites and cottages, a spa and restaurants serving Kashmiri food. The most polished stay in the Lidder valley.
body: Pine N Peak sits along the Lidder on the Aru road corridor, a short drive from the bazaar, with views of forested slopes and snow peaks. It has around 68 rooms across categories including suites and cottages, a spa, and restaurants serving Kashmiri, Indian and international dishes. Service follows ITC's standards, which matter in a town where most hotels are family-run.

It suits signature and upper-comfort travellers, families and honeymooners who want comfort after days in Aru, Betaab Valley and Chandanwari. Union taxis can collect you from the hotel. Book early for April to June and confirm meal plans and room views when booking.
why: The most polished hotel in Pahalgam
Close to the Aru road and Lidder river
Reliable service, spa and Kashmiri dining

faqs.q: Where is Welcomhotel Pine N Peak in Pahalgam?
faqs.a: It is on the Aru road side of Pahalgam, along the Lidder, a short drive from the main bazaar. It is convenient for Aru and the river walks. Union taxis for sightseeing can pick you up at the hotel.

faqs.q: Is Pine N Peak suitable for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes, it has lifts, comfortable rooms and on-site dining, which helps seniors avoid long walks. Request rooms near the lifts and confirm accessibility details when booking.

faqs.q: Is Pine N Peak open in winter?
faqs.a: Large hotels in Pahalgam usually operate through much of the year, but services and access can be limited in deep winter. Check current status and heating before booking December to February.
